what: Dr. Reddy's is an Indian drugmaker. It makes generic versions of medicines once their patents expire, sells branded generics across India and emerging markets, and supplies active ingredients to other manufacturers.
customers: Pharmacy chains and wholesalers in the United States and Europe, doctors and chemists in India and Russia.
money: generic medicines in North America, Europe, India and emerging markets
ingredients and contract manufacturing for others
moat: Regulatory approvals that take years to obtain, manufacturing inspected and cleared by the American and European regulators, and an Indian cost base that few Western makers can match.
risks: Generic prices in the United States fall continuously as more makers enter each molecule
A regulatory inspection failure at one plant can block its products from an entire market
The analyst average target is right where the shares trade, with only five covering it
opportunities: A 12.8% net margin and $678M of cash against $537M of debt
Revenue grew from $2.8B to $3.6B in four years
The Russian consumer health portfolio bought from Haleon adds branded products that do not face generic price erosion
watch: North American generic revenue and whether new product launches offset price erosion.
